Daniel —

Thanks for the heads up. We did run a small set of SKU remaps on 2025-12-29 that adjusted metering for a handful of enterprise customers (mostly EU accounts where we corrected product codes). Those remaps should have been included in the final daily export, but I'll attach our reconciliation spreadsheet so you can cross-check.

Short answers:
- Retroactive SKU corrections: yes (applied 2025-12-29)
- VAT-exempt flags: none were applied by our team for Dec; VAT exemptions for partners started in Jan.

Next steps I propose:
1) We share marketplace_recon_20260112.xlsx with the billing teams (attached).
2) AWS re-runs the invoice calculation and indicates any adjusted tax amounts.
3) If you reissue an amended invoice, please include a short note we can send to our accounting team to justify the change for audit.

Hi all,

Thanks for the recon file and the VAT certificate. We cross-checked your spreadsheet with our metering exports and can confirm:
- The majority of the variance (USD 4,312.45) is due to rounding and SKU remap adjustments you applied on 2025-12-29.
- The 'regional tax adjustment' line was an EU VAT pass-through reclassification; it affects presentation (tax bucket) but not net due for Redwood.

We're preparing a corrected invoice (AWS_Marketplace_Invoice_2025-12_CORRECTED.pdf) which will:
- Show the remap adjustment as a separate credit line with reference code AWS-REM-20251229
- Maintain the same net payable amount (no additional net tax owed by Redwood),
- Include a brief memo: "Adjustment for SKU remapping as requested by seller (Ref: internal reconciliation sheet)."

I'll upload the corrected invoice and a DocuSign acknowledgment link by tomorrow morning. Please confirm once your AP team receives it so we can close the ticket.

Regards,
